aggregate.detectors_note: A detector's denominator (`answerable_for`) is the labelled flags it was answerable for: every flag it spoke on with no `blame` (§5.4's rule that whatever raised an unwanted flag shares the charge), plus the flags whose `blame` named it. A flag whose `blame` named other detectors is not charged here, and one blamed on `score` is in no detector's denominator at all — so these denominators do not sum to the corpus total, by design. `spoke` is the wider count (every flag at this cut whose findings included this detector's) and is shown so the narrow one reads as a share of it. A detector with `g3: null` raised nothing here, which is no evidence rather than a clean bill of health (ADR-001 §7.7); `defaults.never_fired` names them.

tau_sweep.note: §5.4's `F(tau,W)` read at every threshold on the grid, over every episode: the flag population the threshold raises, the `G3` the hand-authored labels can answer for at it, the miss rate it produces, and `unlabelled` — flags nobody has read, which is what refuses to become a rate. This is where a published default is chosen or confirmed from; `thresholds.json` states the bar and the gate, and nowhere else does τ move.

formulas.F(tau,W): risk(e) >= tau, or any finding at severity high
formulas.FP(e): a dismissal whose reason code is in `fp_reasons`
formulas.G3: |{e in F(tau,W): labelled(e) and FP(e)}| / |{e in F(tau,W): labelled(e)}| — ADR-001 §5.4
formulas.TP(e): disposition `accepted`, or rework(e) — see labelling_note. TP is reported beside G3 and is not in its denominator: §5.4's denominator is every labelled flag, true positives and false ones together
formulas.labelling_note: ADR-001 §5.4 names §5.4's four false-positive codes as `expected`, `not-applicable`, `low-stakes` and `false-positive`. The closed list that actually shipped is `e4.6`'s (`fathom_analyze::queue::REASONS`), and the mapping is a collapse, not an invention: §5.4's `expected` is shipped `intentional` ("what looks risky here is what I wanted"); §5.4's `low-stakes` and `false-positive` are shipped under their own names; §5.4's `not-applicable` has no separate shipped code — `false-positive`'s claim ("the finding that raised this does not describe my change") already covers the case, so the two measure together and this file says so instead of hiding the collapse. §5.4's true positive `accepted-with-required-change` is shipped `accepted`: `e4.6`'s ledger has no 'with required change' refinement, so a flag that earned a review that happened is the true positive, and rework of the episode counts as one too per §5.4's own `TP(e)` clause. The five shipped codes that are neither (`not-my-area`, `already-known`, `superseded`, `will-revert`, `other`) are dismissals about the reviewer's attention or the queue's state rather than about the flag: they sit in `G3`'s denominator exactly as §5.4 writes it — the reviewer looked, so the flag cost something — and never in its numerator.
formulas.mature: >= 5 successors on the lineage, or older than 7 days against the pin's clock
formulas.miss_rate: |{e in Mature(W): rework(e) and risk(e) < tau}| / |{e in Mature(W): rework(e)}|
formulas.rework: ADR-001 §5.3 R1|R2|R3 with N = 5; R1's content rung fires at an undo share >= 0.90
formulas.tau_note: §5.4 tightens the *rate* at 1.0 (0.15), not the threshold: tau stays 40 in both gates, so the two `g3-*` gates are one flag set read against two bars. This number moved from 70 to 40 in `reco-6co` and it moved *here*, in ADR-001 §5.4, in the shipped `risk.tau` default, in `fathom.toml` and in the reference policy in the same commit: §5.4 always said its default was to be "confirmed against three real OSS repositories", and the confirmation is this file's own measurement — nothing in 540 real episodes reached 70, so the τ arm of `F(τ,W)` was inert, while τ 40 was the corpus's own top-decile floor and remains the lowest threshold on the grid whose flags are all labelled (see `tau_sweep` in the blessed report). The deciles have moved since — 34 / 42 / 43, two of them above τ, after `reco-0er` lifted every score by taking an absent axis out of the denominator — so what binds τ is the labelling floor, not the deciles. The harness's check against the shipped `risk.tau` is what catches a copy that drifted.

gates.claim: at §5.4's published default τ — 40, confirmed against real history by this corpus in `reco-6co` — the aggregate false-positive rate clears the alpha gate
gates.why: Measured 0.660 (35 false positives on 53 labelled flags) against a bar of 0.30, and the number means something now, which is the difference between this read and `e4.9`'s. At τ 70 the flag arm was inert: 6 episodes in 540 reached it, all six through a high-severity finding and none through τ, because `features-1`'s ceiling on this corpus is 66. τ 40 is §5.4's own \"confirmed against three real OSS repositories\" — it is the shipped `risk.tau`, and the flag population is 53 episodes (9.8 % of the corpus), every one of them carrying a hand-authored disposition. What τ is no longer is the corpus's top-decile floor: the per-repository cuts are 34 / 42 / 43 and two of them now sit above τ, because `reco-0er` lifted every score by taking an absent axis out of the denominator. `aggregate.tau_sweep` is still the evidence and the floor: at τ 35 seven flags have no label, so the rate would be an answer about 56 episodes while 63 were flagged. Read beside `cut_corpus`, the α gate is now the same sentence as the corpus cut rather than a rate over six episodes.

gates.claim: across every episode the corpus flagged — §5.4's published τ plus each repository's own top-decile cut, which is what a reviewer would actually have been shown — no more than 30 % of the labelled flags were cost without value
gates.why: Measured 0.683 on 63 labelled flags: 30 dismissed `low-stakes` (Dependabot, renovate and release-bot bumps, and `update dev dependencies` episodes that re-emit the CI workflow templates and a 1 000-line lockfile — the workflow and dependency axes raised them and no finding justified them — three of the 30 are pin bumps and a dev-dependency refresh that `reco-0er`'s renormalisation lifted over a cut, read again against their own diffs and dismissed again), 10 `false-positive` (a test spy charged as untested new logic twice over, `# type: ignore` and `#[expect(deprecated)]` suppressions whose reason is written on the line above them, a `\"TODO\"` that is the name of a GitHub label, a fuzzer's own report charged as leftover debug output — three labels now, on the same file and the same claim — and mdtest, ty's real test surface, counted as no tests at all twice), 3 `intentional` (the `gh repo garden` deletion that took its test file with it, and dropping Python 3.10 and the other end-of-life Pythons — the two `test_weakening` platform-and-receipt-guard readings `reco-6co` counted in this row now sit below `cli`'s raised cut, so they are out of this count). 24 of the 43 false positives were blamed on the ranking rather than on a detector (`aggregate.coverage.blamed_on_score`) — up from 23, because the band `reco-0er` promoted is entirely ranking-raised; the earlier 26 → 23 was because the two changes `reco-6co` shipped were made to the ranking: a compiled workflow lock is no longer charged the CI weight, and a resolver bot's pin bump no longer makes the operator-action claim at all. The finding still stands and it is still about where the flags come from: the majority of what is left is human-authored maintenance that re-emits CI from an out-of-tree template, which no path rule can see.

gates.claim: the same population clears the 1.0 gate of 0.15
gates.why: 0.683 against 0.15. Written down so that the distance to the 1.0 gate is a measurement and not a vibe: closing it means the flag set stops being mostly routine dependency and template refreshes, which is `e4.4`'s routing and `e4.3`'s catalogue together — the dependency delta saying which pin moved and whether an advisory names it, and a catalogue that knows a regenerated artefact from a hand edit — not one of them alone.

gates.claim: at the published default τ, no more than 20 % of the episodes that later needed rework sat below the flag threshold
gates.why: Measured 0.792: 19 of the 24 mature reworked episodes in the corpus sit below τ 40. At τ 70 this gate measured 1.000 — nothing in 540 episodes reached the published default, so the τ arm of §5.4's `F(τ,W)` did not fire anywhere and the gate was a statement about a threshold nobody reached rather than about recall. Moving τ to the corpus's own decile floor moved the gate from 1.000 to 0.792, which is what the flag arm being live is worth on this history, and it is still four times the bar: what got reworked in these windows was ordinary-looking source edits that the path-and-shape model scores in the 20s and 30s, and no threshold that catches them stops also flagging a fifth of the corpus (`tau_sweep`: τ 25 reaches 13 of the 24 and flags 139 episodes, 25.7 %, and 67 of them nobody has read). This is the companion number §5.4 requires precisely because `G3` alone is satisfied by flagging nothing, and it is the number that says the guardrail's two halves still fail in opposite directions.

gates.claim: at each repository's own top-decile cut — the queue a reviewer would actually have read first — no more than 20 % of the reworked episodes were below it
gates.why: Measured 0.750 (18 of 24). Raising a threshold's strictness is not the same as raising its recall, and this is the number that shows it: even a cut that flags 63 of 540 episodes still misses three quarters of the episodes that later needed rework. It is also where `reco-6co` paid: capping a resolver bot's bump at the dependency claim moved one reworked bump below `cli`'s own cut, so this gate went 0.708 → 0.750 while every other number in the run improved or held. That is the cost of the change and it is written here rather than in a footnote — a bot's bump can be the thing that later needed rework, and a rule that dims the class dims that episode too.

gates.claim: the corpus contains at least 20 mature reworked episodes, which is what a 0.20 gate on a rate needs to be able to tell 0.20 from 0.60
gates.why: Measured 24 out of 525 mature episodes (4.6 %). `e4.9` declared this a `fail` about the corpus, not the product — rework is rare on a healthy repository, and 7 samples cannot discriminate a 0.20 gate — and the fix it named was a bigger pinned window rather than a relaxed threshold. Each pin carries 180 episodes instead of 60 and `astral-sh/ruff` sits at a newer head, which is what clears the floor. Nothing in `thresholds.json`'s bars moved for this gate, and nothing moved for it in `reco-6co` either — the ranking changed, the corpus did not.

gates.claim: every episode any cut flagged has a hand-authored disposition — a flag nobody labelled is a hole in the guardrail, and a guardrail with a hole in it is not a guardrail
gates.why: 63 flags, 63 labels, across all three cuts. A moved ranking promotes episodes nobody has read, and so does a moved denominator: `reco-6co` promoted one (`cli`, `Keep v3.3.0 label for create-github-app-token pin`, 34), and `reco-0zi` promoted five after `reco-0er` lifted every score — a `go-gh` patch bump in `cli`, the `update dev dependencies` refresh in `flask`, and in `ruff` the released-`black` change, a hyperfine bump and the py-fuzzer minimisation budget. All five were labelled against `git show` before this run was blessed. Nine dispositions are printed in `labels_unflagged` — three left by `reco-6co` and six left when `reco-0er` raised `cli`'s cut above episodes that had been in it — and a reading of a diff is not retracted when the score moves, but it is not in a rate either. No label was inferred from a score, a reason distribution or a template. `tests/test_g3_calibration_contract.py` also refuses a label with no note or no evidence, a reason code outside `e4.6`'s closed list, and a label keyed to a commit that is not in its pin's window.

gates.claim: the corpus flags at least 20 episodes, below which `G3` is a story about a handful of commits rather than a rate
gates.why: Measured 63 of 540 episodes — 19 `cli`, 21 `flask`, 23 `ruff`, 11.7 % of the window: the cut is behaving like a rate and not like an accident of one quiet window. This gate exists so that a future re-pin to a quieter window fails loudly instead of turning every ratio gate into `not-measurable` and the suite into a green shrug.

gates.claim: no detector is disqualified by `e0.12`'s rule as this harness scores it: a default-enabled detector whose own false-positive rate breaches the alpha gate on at least 8 answerable flags (the bar a default flip has to clear, deliberately higher than the 5 a printed number has to clear) is a detector that must ship disabled. Read `why` before reading the 0 as a clean bill of health.
gates.why: Measured 0, and the 0 has a mechanism a reader has to know about: `defaults.breaches` asks each detector's *pooled* `g3`, and the pooling step never fills that field — per-repository rates are computed, the aggregate's are not — so every detector that spoke lands in `defaults.under_measured` (its message says \"under the 8 a default flip needs\" even at 11 flags, which is the tell) and the breach count is structurally zero. Scored instead against `aggregate.detectors_corpus`, which recomputes the rate from the pooled offenders and denominators, the corpus sees two default-enabled detectors over α with at least 8 answerable flags: `lint_escape` 0.667 on 9 and `untested_new_logic` 0.556 on 9. `test_weakening` was the third of them at 0.385 on 13 and is 0.273 on 11 now, which is a population moving and not a detector improving — two of its attributed false positives were readings of `cli` episodes that `reco-0er`'s raised cut left below the line, so they left the denominator with the flags. This harness therefore still flips no shipped default in either direction — `e4.3`'s four disabled detectors stay disabled, and `shotgun_edit`, the only disabled detector with a real denominator, measures 0.444 on 9 and does not earn re-enabling — but \"which of those two does `e0.12`'s rule disqualify now\" is a measurable question with an unanswered answer, and it belongs to its own ticket with the weights and the catalogue in it, not to a threshold edit here. `scope_creep`, `secret_string`, `churn_loop` and `rework_loop` still never fired in the corpus, which is no evidence rather than clean (`aggregate.defaults.never_fired` says which).

how_gates_are_set: Every gate declares `expected`: `pass`, `fail` or `not-measurable`. A gate that surprises us in either direction fails the run, because a claim that quietly starts passing has to be re-read just as hard as one that fails. The `fail` gates are the measurement's findings, not its defects: on three real OSS repositories — three windows of 180 episodes each, 540 episodes, 525 of them mature — the shipped score at §5.4's published default τ flags 53 episodes and 35 of them were cost without value, so the α gate measures 0.660; across everything the corpus flags at either cut, 64 → 63 flags of which 43 were cost without value, `G3` 0.683; and 19 of the 24 episodes that were mature and later needed rework still sat below τ, a miss rate of 0.792. Those are the numbers `e0.12`'s thresholds have to survive; they are written here rather than smoothed into a sentence. A gate is never adjusted to fit a measurement: the `min_denominator` floor is what turns an anecdote into `not-measurable` instead of into a comfortable `pass`, and when a gate's `expected` changed it changed because the measurement moved — `miss-rate-denominator-is-big-enough` at the `reco-dyt` re-pin (7 → 24 mature reworked episodes), and `every-flagged-episode-is-labelled` twice, where `reco-6co`'s re-score promoted one episode into the flag population and `reco-0zi`'s re-measure — after `reco-0er` took a guessed `human` out of the score's denominator — promoted five: in both cases the promoted diffs were read and written up before the run was blessed, and the gate came back to `pass`. The bars themselves — 0.30, 0.15, 0.20 — have never moved.
